_comment: No composite indexes: the history screen sorts on one field.
The fieldOverrides are not an optimisation, they are what makes
a write succeed at all. Firestore indexes every field it finds,
including inside arrays, and a document may hold at most 40,000
index entries. A test carries one entry per rep plus one per raw
reading — a 24-rep test with a full session trace runs to several
thousand readings, each a map with its own fields, and the count
multiplies out past the limit. The write then fails outright.
None of it is ever queried. The traces are read back as part of a
document that was found by timestamp, never searched through, so
there is nothing to lose by not indexing them.
